name: CURB-65
seoDesc: CURB-65: work out CURB-65 score from the blood urea nitrogen and the respiratory rate. A free health calculator with the formula, units and a worked example.
summary: Supply the blood urea nitrogen, the respiratory rate, the systolic blood pressure and the diastolic blood pressure and the CURB-65 calculator solves for CURB-65 score. It is built for an informed starting point to take to a clinician, not a diagnosis. The unit chips sit next to the boxes, which is where most hand-calculation mistakes start.

sections.title: How does the CURB-65 calculator work?
sections.html:
The CURB-65 calculator takes the values in the form, applies the relationship described below and reports CURB-65 score in the results panel.

Working from the top of the form: you choose the option that describes your case (confusion?); then you type in the blood urea nitrogen, the respiratory rate, the systolic blood pressure and the diastolic blood pressure.

Press Calculate once and the page holds the relationship, tracking which boxes you filled and working out everything else; from that point on it follows every edit you make.

  • A measured quantity, entered by default in minutes. The unit chip switches it to any of the 27 supported units.
  • A measured quantity, entered by default in millimeters of mercury. The unit chip switches it to any of the 28 supported units.
  • A measured quantity, entered by default in millimeters of mercury. The unit chip switches it to any of the 28 supported units.
  • A number, expressed in years.

sections.title: The formula behind the CURB-65 calculator
sections.html:
The page rests on a handful of relationships. Each one can be rearranged for any of its variables, which is what makes the calculator work in both directions:

CURB-65 score=(confusion? + (age) + (systolic blood pressure, diastolic blood pressure) + (respiratory rate) + (blood urea nitrogen))
Agescore=(age)
Ureascore=(blood urea nitrogen)
Respscore=(respiratory rate)
Bpscore=(systolic blood pressure, diastolic blood pressure)

Read it as an ordinary equation. Where a word appears instead of a letter, it is the label of one of the boxes in the form; where a function appears, it is the usual mathematical meaning of that function.

sections.title: How are units and precision handled?
sections.html:
Units are handled by conversion rather than by convention. Whatever chip you choose, the number is turned into a single base unit before the calculation and rendered back afterwards, so a form filled with a mixture of systems still gives the right answer.

  • Bun – blood urea nitrogen, opening in milligrams per deciliter
  • Time, opening in minutes
  • Pressure, opening in millimeters of mercury
  • Pressure, opening in millimeters of mercury

Display rounding is separate from calculation rounding: the digits you see are shortened, the value behind them is not. Numbers far from everyday size are shown in scientific notation so the significant digits stay readable.

sections.title: When should you use it?
sections.html:
The CURB-65 calculator earns its place in the middle of a task, not instead of one. It is most useful when:

  • Preparing for an appointment so you can describe your numbers clearly
  • Deciding whether a reading is worth a second look
  • Tracking a measurement over time and understanding what changed
  • Any time the same 4 figures keep coming back — the blood urea nitrogen, the respiratory rate and the systolic blood pressure — and you would rather not repeat the arithmetic by hand each time.

sections.title: How do you get a reliable answer?
sections.html:
• Change one input at a time when you are exploring. Two simultaneous changes make it impossible to tell which one moved the result.
  • If a result surprises you, look at the order of magnitude before the digits: a plausible number in the wrong unit looks more convincing than an implausible one, and is easier to miss.
  • Compare two scenarios by changing the input that actually differs between them, and keep the rest fixed, so the difference you see is the difference you meant to test.
  • Write the answer down with its unit. A bare number copied into a report later is exactly where units get lost.

sections.title: What else is worth knowing?
sections.html:
• Answers that depend on a drop-down reflect the option you picked, not a range. Switching to a neighbouring option is the quickest way to see how much that factor matters.
  • Some options are backed by reference tables that ship with the page, so the values are fixed data rather than a live lookup.
  • Fields that are still blank are exactly the ones the calculator has not yet been given, so the results panel is a reliable map of what is missing.

faq.q: What does the CURB-65 calculator work out?
faq.a: It returns CURB-65 score, derived from the blood urea nitrogen, the respiratory rate and the systolic blood pressure. Every field in the form feeds the same relationship: press Calculate once and changing any of them updates the result immediately, with no page reload.

faq.q: What do I need to enter to use the CURB-65 calculator?
faq.a: The form asks for the blood urea nitrogen, the respiratory rate, the systolic blood pressure and the diastolic blood pressure, which is 6 fields in total. Each one is labelled with what it means and, where relevant, the unit it expects. Anything you leave blank is treated as the value to solve for.

faq.q: Can I enter blood urea nitrogen in a different unit?
faq.a: Yes. Blood urea nitrogen opens in milligrams per deciliter and the chip beside it offers 2 units. The number you typed keeps its magnitude and only its label changes; the calculation itself happens in a common base unit, so mixing systems in one form is safe.

faq.q: How much do the drop-down choices change the answer?
faq.a: There is one choice to make (1 in total), and each one selects a different case rather than scaling the result. Switching a single option and watching the result is the fastest way to see how much that choice is worth.

faq.q: Is the CURB-65 calculator free to use?
faq.a: Yes — no account, no sign-up and no limit on how many times you run it. The arithmetic happens in your browser, so the values you type are not sent anywhere.

faq.q: Do I have to fill in every box?
faq.a: Fill in the ones you know. The result boxes are computed from them, so you never enter a value the formula can derive — press Calculate and every result updates together.
